No. The data show 81.3 hectares of tree-cover loss in 2021, or 2.23% of the 3,643.5-hectare property. A further 37.3 hectares of loss occurred in patches smaller than the 0.5-hectare event threshold. Together, these areas represent about 3.3% of the property, not the whole property.

Of the 81.3-hectare event, 68.1 hectares were mapped as planted forest, and none as native forest. Tree-cover loss does not by itself establish the cause or whether the land was permanently cleared.
